metadata.title: Designing an International Large‑Scale Assessment of Professional Competencies and Employability Skills: Emerging Avenues and Challenges of OECD’s PISA‑VET

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This paper is a framework/design discussion of OECD’s PISA‑VET assessment and does not analyze an implemented student dataset. Therefore, no sampling frame, student-level analytic sample, or complex survey weighting variables are applied or reported here. For future PISA‑VET administrations, weighting would be expected to follow the OECD/IEA-style complex survey design logic (stratification and clustering across institutions/programmes), but the manuscript does not specify weight variable names or replicate-weight procedures. The document focuses on target populations, test time constraints, assessment approaches (scenario questions, simulations, live/recorded demonstrations), and contextual/system-level questionnaires rather than on estimation procedures.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: PISA‑VET plausible values (PV) handling is not applicable because this manuscript does not report any student-level achievement scoring, PV generation, or PV-based statistical modeling results. Instead, it outlines the intended assessment framework (occupational areas, employability skills, and assessment approaches) and discusses design challenges and a research agenda. Missing-data handling is not reported because no empirical analysis dataset or estimation model is fitted in this paper.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: No analytic sample is constructed in this paper. The manuscript describes the planned target population (learners near completion of initial VET programmes, typically age 18–20; ISCED 3–4 / EQF 3–4) and the intended occupational areas (automotive technicians, electricians, business and administration, healthcare/nursing assistants, hotel receptionists), but it does not field-test instruments or report participant counts.

data.outcome_summary: This paper does not present empirical ML results; it provides an OECD PISA‑VET assessment and analytical framework design. It targets learners completing initial VET programmes in five occupational areas and proposes a total test time of about 3–4 hours, including questionnaires and breaks. Professional competencies are assessed using a mix of scenario-based questions, digital simulations, and live or recorded demonstrations, while employability skills are operationalized as Literacy, Problem Solving, Task Performance, and Collaboration. The framework also includes system-level data collection and contextual questionnaires (learner, teacher, VET institution leader, and trainers/employers where work-based learning is substantial) to support interpretation and equity/quality analyses. The authors emphasize cross-sectional limitations for causal claims and highlight validity–reliability–feasibility trade-offs inherent in authentic performance assessments.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a framework/design paper rather than an empirical study: it does not report an implemented assessment dataset, student sample sizes, PV generation, missing-data strategy, or any predictive modeling outcomes. Consequently, fields that require empirical estimation inputs (e.g., total_students, countries with n, PV handling details, ML techniques, and main findings) are not populated because there is no fitted model or reported performance metric in the manuscript.
